wu: Warm-up: 'Simon Says' with directions. Teacher says 'Simon says turn left', students turn left; 'Simon says go straight', students march in place. Focus on movement verbs: turn, go, stop.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Draw the Route' - teacher draws a simple path on the board, students call out directions to describe it.
Alternative 2: 'Quick Survey' - students ask each other 'How do you get to class? Bus or walk?' and tally answers.
pres: Presentation: Show a large map of Oujda with key landmarks (Poste, Med V, City Center). Model giving directions: 'Go straight, turn left at the mosque.' Use finger to trace route on map. Check by asking 'Where do I turn?'
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use realia - toy car and street signs to demonstrate movements.
Alternative 2: Draw a simple town map on the board with students naming the places.
prac: Guided practice: 'Map Pairs'. Students get a blank map of Oujda with streets. Student A traces a route with a pencil, Student B writes directions. Teacher circulates to correct prepositions (next to, opposite).
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Flashcard Directions' - students arrange transport flashcards (bus, taxi) to match a spoken route.
Alternative 2: 'Error Correction' - students fix preposition mistakes in a worksheet (e.g., 'turn in the bank' -> 'turn at the bank').
ls: Listening slot: 'Trace the Route'. Students listen to an audio of someone giving directions from the American Space to the train station. They trace the route on their map with a different color crayon. Play twice.
re: Reactivation game: 'Four Corners'. Label corners 'North', 'South', 'East', 'West'. Teacher calls out directions like 'Go to the corner opposite North!', students race there.
prod: Production task: 'Mingle Survey'. Students ask 5 classmates 'How do you get to the souk?' and note answers (walk, taxi, bus). Then, in pairs, they give directions to one of the places mentioned using 'Go straight...'.
rw: Reading and writing slot: 'Order the Directions'. Students read 5 jumbled sentences (e.g., 'Turn right at the pharmacy.', 'Go straight.') and glue them in order on a mini-map worksheet. Then they write 3 directions from their home to the American Space.
st: Story/Song + Goodbye: Sing 'The Wheels on the Bus' with added verses ('The doors on the bus go open and close'). Close with: 'Today we learned to ask for and give directions. Thank you, class.'
g: Teacher says a landmark, students point to it on the map.
Student mimes a direction (turn left), others guess.
Two teams race to trace a correct route on the board.
Students hop to 'next to' the chair, 'opposite' the door.
Students mark transport words called out.
diff: Fast finishers: Draw a map of their neighborhood and write directions to a friend's house.
Support: Use a pre-highlighted map with key words to trace routes.
hw: Homework 1: Write 5 directions from your home to the souk.
Homework 2: Record yourself giving directions to the train station.
Homework 3: Ask a family member for directions to a local place and write them down.
tip: Use landmarks familiar to students (Poste, Med V) to make directions meaningful. Pair strong/weak learners to build confidence.
